title.narrative: Appui d’urgence pour la préparation à la campagne de lutte antiacridienne 2024-25

description.narrative: The island is prone to natural disasters, including drought, floods, cyclones, and locust crises. Over the past few decades, the country has experienced several locust crises of varying severity, including a resurgence in 2010, a resurgence in 2012, an invasion in 2013-2016 and a strong resurgence in 2021-22. The current locust situation, which is considered very critical, comes after a severe drought, the COVID-19 pandemic, Rift Valley fever and Fall armyworm infestations, thus aggravating the situation of food insecurity and malnutrition of vulnerable populations. A Response Programme has been developed jointly by FAO and the Ministry of Agriculture. Four years of locust campaigns will be needed to return to a situation of remission, and this will require $US 21.2 million. The first locust campaign to stop the geographical expansion of locusts is due to start as soon as the first rains arrive, around mid-October 2024; This first campaign is budgeted at $7.3 million. The first activity to be carried out is an in-depth survey to locate locust infestations, which can be identified as soon as the first rains arrive. These observations will make it possible to adjust the intervention strategy and the deployment of teams in the field. In short, this Program aims to contribute to preserving the food security of the most vulnerable rural populations in Madagascar, and is structured around five components, but the CERF project will focus on four components among them, and consists of treating 80,000 ha of locust-infested area. 1. Monitoring and analysis of locust situationsa) Strengthening of data collection and analysis and informationmanagement b) Support for survey operations2. Strengthening locust control(a) Supervision and supervision of human capacity for locust control(b) Support to locust control operations3. Preservation of human health and protection of the environmenta) Human resources for the preservation of human health and protection of the environmentb) Support for monitoring the impact (of treatment) on human health and the environment4. Implementation and coordination of the programmea) Management and coordination of locust emergenciesb) Effective coordination of the responseprogramme The 4 components are interdependent, one cannot go without the other. If an emergency response is not provided, the situation will escalate into a widespread invasion and three-quarters of the island will be infested. Since locusts are a threat to the rural population, this means that about 16 million people will be exposed to the locust threat if left unchecked.
